theme_scores.justification: States a headline target of 30,000 apprenticeships measured 2015-2020 and mentions interim goals, but gives no detail on testing or evaluation timetable.

Describes a concrete process: quarterly data collection coordinated by Cabinet Office, baseline established by end of 2016/17, then annual monitoring, and a legislative target from April 2017, which outlines how progress will be tracked though not why alternatives (testing) are inappropriate or full publication plans.
Names outcomes to be tracked (career progression, retention, grade, organisation) but no timetable, method detail beyond 'interviews and follow-ups', or publication plan.
Lists diversity as a measure from 1 April 2016 but no explanation of methodology, timetable for review, or publication.
Sets a bare goal ('externally recognised... by 2018') with no explanation of how this will be measured or evaluated.
Specifies annual measurement via the People Survey and named benchmarks, but no detail on how results will be used or published.
Mentions employer survey responses on productivity and reliance on contingent labour but no methodology or timetable beyond being 'annual'.
Lists delivery metrics (levels, professions, employer survey) without detail on evaluation process or publication.
States intent to monitor levy spend and utilisation but no explanation of method, frequency beyond implied annual, or publication plan.

reasoning: The extract shows a reasonably developed set of success measures—apprenticeship numbers, diversity, engagement, productivity, quality recognition, and levy spend—organised under 'five main areas' and detailed in an Annex A. The Data Collection theme is the strongest: it specifies quarterly data collection coordinated by the Cabinet Office, a baseline to be established by 'the end of the financial year 2016/17', and progress 'monitored on a financial yearly basis' ahead of 'the legislative target coming into force in April 2017'. This gives some indication of timetable and governance, meeting level 2 criteria for that theme. However, most other themes (targets, tracking, diversity, quality, engagement, productivity, delivery, levy) state what will be measured but not how, why testing/piloting was or wasn't used, or what will happen to results—no mention of publication of findings, or a formal evaluation design. There is no discussion of testing the apprenticeship offer before scaling, nor consultation plans. The document reads as though such detail should exist elsewhere (e.g. Annex A, departmental delivery plans) but it is not shown or cited here. Given only one theme reaches level 2 and the rest cluster at level 1, the section as a whole does not meet 'more comprehensive' across most points. To reach level 2 overall, the document would need to show, for most themes, either developed measurement processes or explicit reasoning against testing/evaluation; to reach level 3 it would need explicit publication and timing commitments tied to a stated rationale.
